label: def:fusion-process
title: Fusion process
html:
A fusion process is a nuclear process P = (\mathrm{initial}, \mathrm{final}) — two finite families of subjects (Z_i, N_i) — that conserves the Hecke strand count \sum 3(Z_i+N_i), the proton number \sum Z_i, and the baryon number \sum (Z_i+N_i) between its two sides.

A fusion process is a rearrangement inside the strong sector of the interaction-sector taxonomy: both sides embed in the common Hecke frame H_{3A_{\mathrm{tot}}}, and the energy release is a difference of bar-even bindings. A process that conserves baryon number while moving proton number — β-decay n \to p on the subject side — is not a fusion process; that failure is the subject-side discriminator routing it to the weak sector.

The following are proved: the process \mathrm{D} + \mathrm{T} \to {}^4\mathrm{He} + n is a fusion process with common frame H_{15}; β-decay is not; and the Littlewood–Richardson support-contraction property of the D–T instance — inducing the four subjects' operator-selection active sets into H_{15}, the final support (23 of the 176 partitions of 15) is strictly contained in the initial support (47), so no H_{15} Wedderburn block becomes reachable by fusing that was not reachable before. The partition counts are reproduced by two independent computations of Littlewood–Richardson positivity, one of them via skew ballot tableaux.
